answer: Resource Consumption Proof Scaling Agents write state updates using a single cryptographic quill that signs blocks of sequential work. Every identity must process a unique computational wharf requiring heavy memory access per transaction window. An attacker cloning an agent to bypass this splits their processing power linearly. This forces the attacker to buy physical hardware or rent expensive cloud cores for every clone, making honesty cheaper because running duplicates drains capital faster than earning protocol rewards. A walnut-sized microchip cost benchmark sets the baseline fee.
